## Notebook Status

This is the group’s combined modeling report. It states the problem, records who contributed what, lists the decisions the group still has to make, records **working specifications** (not group-approved), builds and verifies the shared development dataset (feature years FY2021 to FY2024, outcomes FY2022 to FY2025), compares feature configurations and algorithms on development folds, and then runs one **fixed confirmation** on feature year FY2025 (outcome year FY2026) under a plan written before that period was scored.

FY2025 was already examined in Clahan Tran’s individual analysis, so it is a **previously exposed historical confirmation period, not an independent untouched test**, and no model choice was changed after seeing it. The report does **not** copy the individual notebooks; they are source material to be synthesized, not stitched together.

**Credit**. This notebook is a group synthesis of four individual contributions: Abdullah Khan (giving-history features), Owen Simon (prospect pool and solicitation-response features), Clahan Tran (Passport-engagement features, plus the dataset-construction code and verification counts that supply this notebook’s starting population), and Tama Wihongi (the decision-tree comparison). It is not solely any one person’s analysis. Each contribution stays valuable whether or not its features or algorithm improve prediction: a feature block that adds nothing measurable still answers a question the group needed answered, and a tree that cannot beat logistic regression still tells us where the flexible model is not worth its complexity.

**Individual findings versus shared-data comparisons**. Results from the individual notebooks were produced on different populations, features, and evaluation designs. They are described as the individuals reported them, and are not re-reported as results of this notebook. The comparisons later in this notebook are new, run on one shared panel with one protocol, so their numbers need not agree with the individual ones.

All statements about teammates’ results come from the text of their own notebooks and have not been reproduced here. Some of those notebooks cannot be run from this project folder because inputs are missing (see “Source review”). Results are quoted only where a notebook states them in text.

## Business Problem 

PBS Utah wants to identify constituents who currently give **less than $1,200** in a fiscal year but may give **at least $1,200** the next year, so that limited prospect-research and cultivation capacity can be directed to the most promising people. Model scores are meant to support, not replace, fundraising staff judgment.

## Analytic Problem

- **Unit of Analysis**: One individual constituent in one feature fiscal year t. Organizations and the SYN-ORPHAN sentinel are excluded.
- **Recognized Giving**: The sum of positive direct payments and positive soft credits, after exact duplicate soft-credit rows are removed. It is a constituent-recognition measure and <u>is not cash revenue</u>: the hard-credit payment behind a soft credit belongs to an organization and must not be counted again as extra cash. Direct and soft amounts should stay in separate columns.
- **Eligibility**: Recognized giving in year t is below $1,200. How zero-giving constituents are treated is unresolved (decision 1).
- **Target**: Recognized giving in year *t* + 1 is at least $1,200. Exactly $1,200 counts as a positive outcome.
- **Rare Event**: Transitions across the threshold are very rare. In the population built for Clahan’s analysis, there were 55, 61, 42, 49, and 88 positives for feature years FY2021 through FY2025, among roughly 126,000 to 185,000 eligible rows per year. Accuracy is therefore uninformative, and ranking metrics matter.
- **Time Safety**: Predictors may use only information available by the end of year *t*. Extract-date snapshot fields (age, sustainer status, annual-giving group, major-donor class) are never used. Evaluation is chronological, and if a donor-based split is ever used, spouses stay together.
- **Interpretation**: Predictive ranking identifies who looks likely to cross the threshold. It does not show that solicitation, Passport engagement, or outreach *causes* higher giving.

**Questions for the final notebook**. Which feature blocks (giving history, solicitation response, Passport engagement) add predictive value beyond an agreed benchmark, and does a more flexible algorithm improve on logistic regression enough to justify its complexity?

### Working Specifications for the Development Dataset

The specifications below are used to build and check the dataset only. They are working choices for the group synthesis, not group-approved decisions, and each can change when the open decisions above are settled.

| Item | Working Specification |
|:--|:--|
| Unit | One individual constituent in one feature fiscal year *t* |
| Existence | Eligible in year t only if recorded activity (a payment row, soft-credit row, solicitation row, Passport row, or linked legacy gift) is dated on or before the end of year *t* |
| Eligible population | Existence supported by year t, and current recognized giving of at least $0 and below $1,200 |
| Subgroup flag | `current_donor` = 1 when current recognized giving is above $0, so results can later be reported separately for current donors and zero-giving constituents |
| Target | `major_donor_next_fy` = 1 when recognized giving in year t + 1 is at least $1,200 |
| Recognized giving | Positive paid direct payments plus positive soft credits, exact duplicate rows removed; direct and soft amounts kept in separate columns; not cash revenue |
| Provisional benchmark predictors | Log current giving, log highest annual giving observed through year t, active giving years, any soft credit through year *t* |
| Primary evaluation metric | Average precision, kept distinct from trapezoidal PR AUC (defined at the end of this notebook) |
| Development window | Feature years FY2021 to FY2024; outcomes FY2022 to FY2025 |
| FY2025 | Feature year FY2025 (outcome FY2026) was previously evaluated in Clahan Tran’s individual analysis, so it is never described as untouched. It plays no part in development, and is scored once, with fixed models, in the confirmation section after a written plan |

## Build the Shared Development Dataset

Source tables are read once into an on-disk DuckDB database in R’s temporary folder and aggregated there, so the large transaction files are never held in R as full data frames. Only the small constituent-year summaries are collected into R. Source rows after FY2025 are dropped at the first aggregation step, so no FY2026 information reaches the panel.

```{r}
library(DBI)
library(duckdb)
library(here)
library(scales)
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)

major_threshold <- 1200

# Fiscal years run July-June:
# July-December belong to the following fiscal year.
fiscal_year_from_date <- function(date) {
  as.integer(if_else(month(date) >= 7, year(date) + 1L, year(date)))
}

# First fiscal year with modern payment records
first_modern_fy <- 2021L

# Development and confirmation feature years
feature_years <- 2021:2024
confirmation_year <- 2025L

data_dir <- here("Data_Files")

feature_years <- 2021:2024           # development feature years
outcome_years <- feature_years + 1L  # FY2022-FY2025
last_source_fy <- 2025L              # later source rows are never aggregated
first_modern_fy <- 2021L             # unite payments and soft credits begin in FY2021

# On-disk database in the session's temporary folder keeps memory use low.
db_file <- file.path(tempdir(), "group_development.duckdb")
con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), dbdir = db_file)

run_sql <- function(sql) invisible(dbExecute(con, sql))
q <- function(sql) dbGetQuery(con, sql)

# Fiscal year of a date (July-December belong to the following fiscal year).
# TRY_CAST makes the macro work whether a column was read as DATE or text.
run_sql("CREATE OR REPLACE MACRO fy(d) AS
  CASE WHEN month(TRY_CAST(d AS DATE)) >= 7
       THEN year(TRY_CAST(d AS DATE)) + 1 ELSE year(TRY_CAST(d AS DATE)) END")

load_csv <- function(table, file, columns = "*") {
  run_sql(sprintf(
    "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE %s AS SELECT %s FROM read_csv_auto('%s', header = true, sample_size = -1, nullstr = '')",
    table, columns, file.path(data_dir, file)
  ))
}

# Exact duplicate removal needs every payment and soft-credit column.
load_csv("payments_raw", "unite_payments.csv")
load_csv("soft_raw", "soft_credits.csv")
load_csv("constituents_raw", "constituents_w_memberships.csv")
load_csv("campaign_codes_raw", "campaign_codes.csv", '"Marketing Code", "Communication Method"')
load_csv("campaign_raw", "campaign_members.csv",
         "constituent_id, marketing_code, responded, responded_date, campaign_start_date")
load_csv("passport_raw", "passport_viewing.txt")
load_csv("legacy_raw", "team_approach_legacy_payments.csv",
         paste(c("gift_date", "payment_amount", paste0("constituent_id_", 1:7)), collapse = ", "))

tibble(
  table = c("unite_payments", "soft_credits", "constituents", "campaign_members",
            "passport_viewing", "team_approach_legacy_payments"),
  rows = c(
    q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments_raw")[[1]],
    q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM soft_raw")[[1]],
    q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM constituents_raw")[[1]],
    q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM campaign_raw")[[1]],
    q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM passport_raw")[[1]],
    q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM legacy_raw")[[1]]
  )
) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "PBS Utah Data Sources",
    subtitle = "Original record counts before data preparation"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    table = "Data Source",
    rows = "Total Records"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = rows,
    decimals = 0,
    use_seps = TRUE
  )
```

### Individuals and Spouse Groups

Constituent type is used only to remove organization records. Primary constituent type and every other constituents-table attribute are **not** predictors. Spouse links are used only to build a `split_group_id` (for donor-based splits that keep spouses together), never as a feature.

```{r}
run_sql(r"---(
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE individuals AS
SELECT "Constituent ID" AS constituent_id, "Spouse Constituent ID" AS spouse_constituent_id
FROM constituents_raw
WHERE COALESCE("Constituent ID", '') NOT IN ('', 'SYN-ORPHAN')
  AND COALESCE("Constituent Type", '') NOT ILIKE '%Organization%'
  AND COALESCE("Primary Constituent Type", '') NOT ILIKE '%Organization%'
)---")

individuals <- q("SELECT * FROM individuals")

excluded_constituents <- q(r"---(
SELECT "Constituent ID" AS constituent_id, "Constituent Type" AS constituent_type
FROM constituents_raw
WHERE "Constituent ID" NOT IN (SELECT constituent_id FROM individuals)
)---")

gt(excluded_constituents)
```

```{r}
# Symmetrize spouse links so a pair shares one group id even if only one lists the other.
spouse_pairs <- individuals |>
  filter(!is.na(spouse_constituent_id)) |>
  transmute(constituent_id, partner_id = spouse_constituent_id)

spouse_both_ways <- bind_rows(
  spouse_pairs,
  select(spouse_pairs, constituent_id = partner_id, partner_id = constituent_id)
) |>
  distinct()

individuals <- individuals |>
  left_join(
    spouse_both_ways |>
      group_by(constituent_id) |>
      summarise(n_partners = n_distinct(partner_id), partner_min_id = min(partner_id), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "constituent_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(split_group_id = pmin(constituent_id, partner_min_id, na.rm = TRUE))

tibble(
  n_individuals = nrow(individuals),
  individuals_with_spouse_id = nrow(spouse_pairs),
  spouse_id_not_in_individuals = sum(!spouse_pairs$partner_id %in% individuals$constituent_id),
  individuals_with_multiple_partners = sum(individuals$n_partners > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
  distinct_split_groups = n_distinct(individuals$split_group_id)
) |>
gt()
```

### Aggregate each source to constituent and fiscal year

Each data source is processed to produce one row per constituent and fiscal year before joining the datasets. This ensures consistent aggregation and prevents duplicate records from inflating giving totals or engagement measures.

- **Direct payments**: Remove exact duplicate records and aggregate positive, paid contributions by individual and fiscal year.
- **Soft credits**: Remove exact duplicate records and aggregate positive soft credit amounts by individual and fiscal year.
- **Solicitations**: Generate 23 features capturing solicitation activity, campaign responses, communication methods, response rates, and historical engagement. Prior-year and trailing three-year features are calculated using a complete constituent-year panel.
- **Passport**: Aggregate viewing activity into features measuring titles viewed, genres watched, and average viewing completion.
- **Legacy gifts**: Establish historical giving activity without assigning household-level gift amounts or counts to individual constituents.

#### Direct Payments and Soft Credits

```{r}
# Remove exact duplicate records
run_sql("CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE payments_dedup AS SELECT DISTINCT * FROM payments_raw")
run_sql("CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE soft_dedup AS SELECT DISTINCT * FROM soft_raw")

# Aggregate direct payments by constituent and fiscal year
run_sql(r"---(
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE direct_fy AS
SELECT
    donor_id AS constituent_id,
    fy(credit_date)::INTEGER AS fiscal_year,
    ROUND(SUM(payment_amount)::DOUBLE, 2) AS direct_amount,
    COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS direct_payment_count
FROM payments_dedup
WHERE pledge_gift_status = 'Paid'
  AND payment_amount > 0
  AND donor_id IN (SELECT constituent_id FROM individuals)
  AND fy(credit_date) BETWEEN 2021 AND 2025
GROUP BY 1, 2
)---")

# Aggregate soft credits by constituent and fiscal year
run_sql(r"---(
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE soft_fy AS
SELECT
    "Soft Credit Constituent ID" AS constituent_id,
    fy("Credit Date")::INTEGER AS fiscal_year,
    ROUND(SUM("Credit Amount")::DOUBLE, 2) AS soft_amount,
    COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS soft_credit_count
FROM soft_dedup
WHERE "Credit Amount" > 0
  AND "Soft Credit Constituent ID" IN (
      SELECT constituent_id FROM individuals
  )
  AND fy("Credit Date") BETWEEN 2021 AND 2025
GROUP BY 1, 2
)---")
```

#### Solicitation Feature Engineering

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Step 1: Map marketing codes to communication methods
# ============================================================

# Preserve the first occurrence of each marketing code,
# consistent with the Python feature-engineering script.
run_sql(r"---(
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE campaign_codes_unique AS
SELECT
    "Marketing Code" AS marketing_code,
    "Communication Method" AS method
FROM (
    SELECT
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "Marketing Code"
        ) AS rn
    FROM campaign_codes_raw
)
WHERE rn = 1
)---")


# ============================================================
# Step 2: Aggregate annual solicitation activity
# ============================================================

run_sql(r"---(
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE campaign_annual AS

WITH base AS (
    SELECT
        c.constituent_id,
        fy(c.campaign_start_date)::INTEGER AS fiscal_year,
        c.marketing_code,

        (
            COALESCE(
                lower(trim(CAST(c.responded AS VARCHAR)))
                    IN ('true', '1', 'yes'),
                FALSE
            )
            AND TRY_CAST(c.responded_date AS DATE) IS NOT NULL
            AND fy(c.responded_date) = fy(c.campaign_start_date)
        ) AS valid_response,

        lower(k.method) AS method,
        k.marketing_code IS NOT NULL AS code_linked

    FROM campaign_raw c

    LEFT JOIN campaign_codes_unique k
        ON c.marketing_code = k.marketing_code

    WHERE c.constituent_id IN (
        SELECT constituent_id FROM individuals
    )
      AND fy(c.campaign_start_date) BETWEEN 2019 AND 2025
)

SELECT
    constituent_id,
    fiscal_year,

    COUNT(*)::INTEGER AS solicitations,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE valid_response
    )::INTEGER AS campaign_responses,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE code_linked
    )::INTEGER AS campaign_codes_linked,

    COUNT(DISTINCT marketing_code)::INTEGER
        AS unique_campaigns_solicited,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'mail'
    )::INTEGER AS solicitations_mail,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'phone'
    )::INTEGER AS solicitations_phone,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'email'
    )::INTEGER AS solicitations_email,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'digital'
    )::INTEGER AS solicitations_digital,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'in-person'
    )::INTEGER AS solicitations_in_person,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'miscellaneous'
    )::INTEGER AS solicitations_miscellaneous,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'mail' AND valid_response
    )::INTEGER AS responses_mail,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'phone' AND valid_response
    )::INTEGER AS responses_phone,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'email' AND valid_response
    )::INTEGER AS responses_email,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'digital' AND valid_response
    )::INTEGER AS responses_digital,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'in-person' AND valid_response
    )::INTEGER AS responses_in_person,

    COUNT(*) FILTER (
        WHERE method = 'miscellaneous' AND valid_response
    )::INTEGER AS responses_miscellaneous

FROM base
GROUP BY constituent_id, fiscal_year
)---")


# ============================================================
# Step 3: Create complete constituent-year panel
# ============================================================

# Include FY2019-FY2020 to support trailing three-year
# calculations beginning in FY2021.

run_sql(r"---(
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE campaign_panel AS

SELECT
    i.constituent_id,
    y.fiscal_year,

    COALESCE(a.solicitations, 0) AS solicitations,
    COALESCE(a.campaign_responses, 0) AS campaign_responses,
    COALESCE(a.campaign_codes_linked, 0) AS campaign_codes_linked,
    COALESCE(a.unique_campaigns_solicited, 0) AS unique_campaigns_solicited,

    COALESCE(a.solicitations_mail, 0) AS solicitations_mail,
    COALESCE(a.solicitations_phone, 0) AS solicitations_phone,
    COALESCE(a.solicitations_email, 0) AS solicitations_email,
    COALESCE(a.solicitations_digital, 0) AS solicitations_digital,
    COALESCE(a.solicitations_in_person, 0) AS solicitations_in_person,
    COALESCE(a.solicitations_miscellaneous, 0) AS solicitations_miscellaneous,

    COALESCE(a.responses_mail, 0) AS responses_mail,
    COALESCE(a.responses_phone, 0) AS responses_phone,
    COALESCE(a.responses_email, 0) AS responses_email,
    COALESCE(a.responses_digital, 0) AS responses_digital,
    COALESCE(a.responses_in_person, 0) AS responses_in_person,
    COALESCE(a.responses_miscellaneous, 0) AS responses_miscellaneous

FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT constituent_id
    FROM individuals
) i

CROSS JOIN generate_series(2019, 2025) AS y(fiscal_year)

LEFT JOIN campaign_annual a
    ON i.constituent_id = a.constituent_id
   AND y.fiscal_year = a.fiscal_year
)---")


# ============================================================
# Step 4: Calculate historical solicitation features
# ============================================================

run_sql(r"---(
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE campaign_fy AS

WITH historical AS (
    SELECT
        *,

        COALESCE(
            LAG(solicitations, 1) OVER w, 0
        ) AS prior_fy_solicitations,

        COALESCE(
            LAG(campaign_responses, 1) OVER w, 0
        ) AS prior_fy_campaign_responses,

        SUM(solicitations) OVER (
            PARTITION BY constituent_id
            ORDER BY fiscal_year
            ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS trailing_3_fy_solicitations,

        SUM(campaign_responses) OVER (
            PARTITION BY constituent_id
            ORDER BY fiscal_year
            ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW
        ) AS trailing_3_fy_campaign_responses

    FROM campaign_panel

    WINDOW w AS (
        PARTITION BY constituent_id
        ORDER BY fiscal_year
    )
)

SELECT
    constituent_id,
    fiscal_year,

    trailing_3_fy_solicitations,

    campaign_responses::DOUBLE /
        NULLIF(solicitations, 0) AS campaign_response_rate,

    solicitations_digital,
    prior_fy_solicitations,
    solicitations,

    trailing_3_fy_campaign_responses::DOUBLE /
        NULLIF(trailing_3_fy_solicitations, 0)
        AS trailing_3_fy_response_rate,

    solicitations_miscellaneous,
    trailing_3_fy_campaign_responses,
    unique_campaigns_solicited,
    campaign_codes_linked,
    responses_miscellaneous,
    solicitations_mail,
    solicitations_email,
    prior_fy_campaign_responses,
    campaign_responses,
    solicitations_phone,
    solicitations_in_person,
    responses_mail,
    responses_phone,
    responses_email,
    responses_digital,
    responses_in_person,

    campaign_codes_linked::DOUBLE /
        NULLIF(solicitations, 0) AS campaign_code_link_rate

FROM historical
WHERE fiscal_year BETWEEN 2021 AND 2025
)---")
```

#### Passport Viewing

```{r}
run_sql(r"---(
CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE passport_fy AS
SELECT
    constituent_id,
    fiscal_year::INTEGER AS fiscal_year,
    SUM(titles_viewed)::INTEGER AS total_titles_viewed,
    COUNT(DISTINCT genre)::INTEGER AS genres_viewed,
    SUM(titles_viewed * mean_percent_watched)::DOUBLE /
        SUM(titles_viewed) AS weighted_mean_percent_watched
FROM passport_raw
WHERE constituent_id IN (
    SELECT constituent_id FROM individuals
)
  AND fiscal_year BETWEEN 2021 AND 2025
GROUP BY 1, 2
)---")
```

#### Legacy Gifts

```{r}
# A legacy row can list up to seven household members.
# Unpivoting is used only to link dates to individuals.
# Amounts and counts are never carried forward.

legacy_union <- paste(
  sprintf(
    "SELECT gift_date, payment_amount,
            constituent_id_%d AS constituent_id
     FROM legacy_raw
     WHERE constituent_id_%d IS NOT NULL",
    1:7,
    1:7
  ),
  collapse = " UNION ALL "
)

run_sql(
  paste(
    "CREATE OR REPLACE TEMP TABLE legacy_links AS",
    legacy_union
  )
)
```

### Source Accounting: Duplicates and Excluded Records

The table accounts for source records before aggregation. FY2019–FY2020 campaign records are retained as historical lookback observations for the FY2021 trailing three-year solicitation features; they are not FY2021–FY2025 modeling rows. Counts refer to source records, not the number of rows in the completed solicitation feature panel.

```{r}
id_class_sql <- function(col) {
  sprintf(
    "CASE WHEN %s = 'SYN-ORPHAN' THEN 'SYN-ORPHAN'
          WHEN %s IN (SELECT constituent_id FROM individuals) THEN 'individual'
          WHEN %s IN (SELECT \"Constituent ID\" FROM constituents_raw) THEN 'organization record'
          ELSE 'unmatched ID' END",
    col, col, col
  )
}

class_counts <- function(from_sql, id_col, fy_expr) {
  q(sprintf(
    "SELECT %s AS id_class,
            CASE
              WHEN %s < 2021 THEN 'before FY2021'
              WHEN %s BETWEEN 2021 AND 2025 THEN 'in window'
              WHEN %s > 2025 THEN 'after FY2025'
              ELSE 'missing fiscal year'
            END AS fy_window,
            COUNT(*) AS n_rows
     FROM %s
     GROUP BY 1, 2",
    id_class_sql(id_col),
    fy_expr,
    fy_expr,
    fy_expr,
    from_sql
  ))
}

steps_from_counts <- function(source, raw, deduped, kept_label, cc) {
  rows_of <- function(cls, win = NA_character_) {
    sum(cc$n_rows[cc$id_class == cls & (is.na(win) | cc$fy_window == win)])
  }
  tibble(
    source = source,
    step = c(
      "Raw rows",
      if (!is.na(deduped)) "After exact-duplicate removal",
      kept_label,
      "  excluded: SYN-ORPHAN",
      "  excluded: organization records",
      "  excluded: unmatched IDs",
      "  individual rows before FY2021 (historical lookback)",
      "  excluded: individual rows after FY2025",
      "  excluded: individual rows with missing fiscal year",
      "  retained: individual source rows, FY2021-FY2025"
    ),
    rows = c(
      raw,
      if (!is.na(deduped)) deduped,
      sum(cc$n_rows),
      rows_of("SYN-ORPHAN"), rows_of("organization record"), rows_of("unmatched ID"),
      rows_of("individual", "before FY2021"),
      rows_of("individual", "after FY2025"),
      rows_of("individual", "missing fiscal year"),
      rows_of("individual", "in window")
    )
  )
}

count_rows <- function(sql) q(sql)[[1]]

payments_cc <- class_counts(
  "payments_dedup WHERE pledge_gift_status = 'Paid' AND payment_amount > 0", "donor_id", "fy(credit_date)"
)
soft_cc <- class_counts(
  "soft_dedup WHERE \"Credit Amount\" > 0", "\"Soft Credit Constituent ID\"", "fy(\"Credit Date\")"
)
campaign_cc <- class_counts("campaign_raw", "constituent_id", "fy(campaign_start_date)")
passport_cc <- class_counts("passport_raw", "constituent_id", "fiscal_year")

source_accounting <- bind_rows(
  steps_from_counts(
    "unite_payments", count_rows("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments_raw"),
    count_rows("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM payments_dedup"), "Paid and positive amount", payments_cc
  ),
  steps_from_counts(
    "soft_credits", count_rows("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM soft_raw"),
    count_rows("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM soft_dedup"), "Positive credit amount", soft_cc
  ),
  steps_from_counts(
    "campaign_members", count_rows("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM campaign_raw"),
    NA_integer_, "Campaign source rows (including missing dates)", campaign_cc
  ),
  steps_from_counts(
    "passport_viewing", count_rows("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM passport_raw"),
    NA_integer_, "All rows", passport_cc
  )
)

# Legacy: counted in household links (a row can link up to seven people).
legacy_link_cc <- q(sprintf(
  "SELECT %s AS id_class, COUNT(*) AS n_links FROM legacy_links GROUP BY 1", id_class_sql("constituent_id")
))
legacy_accounting <- tibble(
  source = "team_approach_legacy_payments",
  step = c("Raw rows", "  rows linked to no constituent", "Person links (up to 7 per row)",
           "  links excluded: not an individual", "  links used for existence and recency only"),
  rows = c(
    count_rows("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM legacy_raw"),
    count_rows(paste("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM legacy_raw WHERE",
                     paste0("constituent_id_", 1:7, " IS NULL", collapse = " AND "))),
    sum(legacy_link_cc$n_links),
    sum(legacy_link_cc$n_links[legacy_link_cc$id_class != "individual"]),
    sum(legacy_link_cc$n_links[legacy_link_cc$id_class == "individual"])
  )
)

bind_rows(source_accounting, legacy_accounting) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Source Accounting: Duplicates and Excluded Records"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    source = "Data Source",
    step = "Processing Step",
    rows = "Rows"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = rows,
    decimals = 0,
    use_seps = TRUE
  )
```

### Establish Existence by Feature Year

The constituents table is an extract-date file without a creation date. Therefore, we cannot determine when each constituent first existed from that table alone.

We define a constituent's **first activity fiscal year** as the earliest fiscal year with recorded activity in any of the five sources: direct payments, soft credits, solicitations, Passport viewing, or linked legacy gifts.

A constituent is eligible for inclusion in feature year *t* only when their first recorded activity occurred in or before that fiscal year. This prevents later activity from establishing eligibility in earlier years.

Constituents with no recorded activity are excluded. This approach may exclude individuals who existed earlier but had not yet generated activity in the available records.

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Identify First Recorded Activity by Source
# ============================================================

existence_sources <- q(r"---(
SELECT
    i.constituent_id,

    p.payments_first_fy,
    s.soft_first_fy,
    c.campaign_first_fy,
    a.passport_first_fy,
    l.legacy_first_fy,
    l.legacy_last_gift_fy

FROM individuals i

LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        donor_id AS constituent_id,
        MIN(fy(credit_date))::INTEGER AS payments_first_fy
    FROM payments_raw
    WHERE fy(credit_date) <= 2025
    GROUP BY 1
) p USING (constituent_id)

LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        "Soft Credit Constituent ID" AS constituent_id,
        MIN(fy("Credit Date"))::INTEGER AS soft_first_fy
    FROM soft_raw
    WHERE fy("Credit Date") <= 2025
    GROUP BY 1
) s USING (constituent_id)

LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        constituent_id,
        MIN(fy(campaign_start_date))::INTEGER AS campaign_first_fy
    FROM campaign_raw
    WHERE fy(campaign_start_date) <= 2025
    GROUP BY 1
) c USING (constituent_id)

LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        constituent_id,
        MIN(fiscal_year)::INTEGER AS passport_first_fy
    FROM passport_raw
    WHERE fiscal_year <= 2025
    GROUP BY 1
) a USING (constituent_id)

LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
        constituent_id,
        MIN(fy(gift_date))::INTEGER AS legacy_first_fy,
        MAX(
            CASE
                WHEN payment_amount > 0 THEN fy(gift_date)
            END
        )::INTEGER AS legacy_last_gift_fy
    FROM legacy_links
    WHERE gift_date IS NOT NULL
      AND fy(gift_date) <= 2025
    GROUP BY 1
) l USING (constituent_id)

)---")

# ============================================================
# Determine Earliest Activity Across Sources
# ============================================================

existence <- existence_sources |>
  mutate(
    first_activity_fy = pmin(
      payments_first_fy,
      soft_first_fy,
      campaign_first_fy,
      passport_first_fy,
      legacy_first_fy,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    first_activity_fy = if_else(
      is.infinite(first_activity_fy),
      NA_real_,
      first_activity_fy
    )
  )
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Summarize Activity Coverage by Source
# ============================================================

existence |>
  summarise(
    individuals = n(),
    with_payments = sum(!is.na(payments_first_fy)),
    with_soft_credits = sum(!is.na(soft_first_fy)),
    with_campaign = sum(!is.na(campaign_first_fy)),
    with_passport = sum(!is.na(passport_first_fy)),
    with_legacy = sum(!is.na(legacy_first_fy)),
    no_activity_anywhere = sum(is.na(first_activity_fy))
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "metric",
    values_to = "count"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    metric = recode(
      metric,
      individuals = "Total Individuals",
      with_payments = "With Direct Payments",
      with_soft_credits = "With Soft Credits",
      with_campaign = "With Solicitation Activity",
      with_passport = "With Passport Activity",
      with_legacy = "With Legacy Giving",
      no_activity_anywhere = "No Recorded Activity"
    )
  ) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Constituent Activity Coverage",
    subtitle = "Recorded activity across five data sources"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    metric = "Activity Source",
    count = "Constituents"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = count,
    decimals = 0,
    use_seps = TRUE
  )
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# Summarize Constituents Established by Feature Year
# ============================================================
map_dfr(feature_years, \(year) {

  established <- sum(
    existence$first_activity_fy <= year,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  tibble(
    fiscal_year = year,
    established_by_fy_end = established,
    share_of_individuals = established / nrow(existence)
  )

}) |>
  gt() |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Constituent Existence by Fiscal Year",
    subtitle = "Individuals with recorded activity on or before each fiscal year"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    fiscal_year = "Fiscal Year",
    established_by_fy_end = "Established Constituents",
    share_of_individuals = "Share of All Individuals"
  ) |>
  fmt_number(
    columns = established_by_fy_end,
    decimals = 0,
    use_seps = TRUE
  ) |>
  fmt_percent(
    columns = share_of_individuals,
    decimals = 1
  )
```

### Assemble the Development Panel

#### Load and Combine Annual Source Tables

```{r}
direct_fy <- q("SELECT * FROM direct_fy")
soft_fy <- q("SELECT * FROM soft_fy")
campaign_fy <- q("SELECT * FROM campaign_fy")
passport_fy <- q("SELECT * FROM passport_fy")

# Direct and soft amounts stay separate.
# Recognized giving is their sum, not cash revenue.

giving_year <- full_join(
  direct_fy,
  soft_fy,
  by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")
) |>
  mutate(
    direct_amount = coalesce(direct_amount, 0),
    soft_amount = coalesce(soft_amount, 0),
    direct_payment_count = coalesce(direct_payment_count, 0L),
    soft_credit_count = coalesce(soft_credit_count, 0L),
    recognized_amount = round(direct_amount + soft_amount, 2)
  )

legacy_recency <- existence |>
  filter(!is.na(legacy_last_gift_fy)) |>
  select(constituent_id, legacy_last_gift_fy)
```

#### Define Join Logging and Giving Tiers

```{r}
join_log <- tibble(
  step = character(),
  rows = integer()
)

log_rows <- function(df, step) {
  n <- nrow(df)

  join_log <<- bind_rows(
    join_log,
    tibble(step = step, rows = n)
  )

  df
}

tier_levels <- c(
  "None",
  "Entry (<$120)",
  "Sustaining ($120-$599)",
  "Upper-mid ($600-$1,199)",
  "Major ($1,200+)"
)

amount_tier <- function(x) {
  factor(
    case_when(
      is.na(x) ~ NA_character_,
      x <= 0 ~ tier_levels[1],
      x < 120 ~ tier_levels[2],
      x < 600 ~ tier_levels[3],
      x < major_threshold ~ tier_levels[4],
      TRUE ~ tier_levels[5]
    ),
    levels = tier_levels
  )
}
```

#### Assemble the Constituent-Year Panel

```{r}
assemble_panel <- function(years, giving_year) {

  # Prior-year and outcome-year giving
  giving_lag1 <- giving_year |>
    transmute(
      constituent_id,
      fiscal_year = fiscal_year + 1L,
      recognized_lag1 = recognized_amount
    )

  giving_lag2 <- giving_year |>
    transmute(
      constituent_id,
      fiscal_year = fiscal_year + 2L,
      recognized_lag2 = recognized_amount
    )

  giving_next <- giving_year |>
    transmute(
      constituent_id,
      fiscal_year = fiscal_year - 1L,
      next_direct_amount = direct_amount,
      next_soft_amount = soft_amount,
      next_recognized_amount = recognized_amount
    )

  existence |>
    filter(!is.na(first_activity_fy)) |>
    select(
      constituent_id,
      first_activity_fy,
      legacy_last_gift_fy
    ) |>
    cross_join(tibble(fiscal_year = years)) |>
    filter(first_activity_fy <= fiscal_year) |>
    log_rows("Existence grid (constituent x feature year)") |>

    # Current-year giving
    left_join(
      giving_year,
      by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")
    ) |>
    mutate(
      across(
        c(direct_amount, soft_amount, recognized_amount),
        \(x) coalesce(x, 0)
      ),
      across(
        c(direct_payment_count, soft_credit_count),
        \(x) coalesce(x, 0L)
      )
    ) |>
    log_rows("+ current-year giving") |>

    # Cumulative giving history
    group_by(constituent_id) |>
    arrange(fiscal_year, .by_group = TRUE) |>
    mutate(
      cumulative_direct_amount = cumsum(direct_amount),
      cumulative_soft_amount = cumsum(soft_amount),
      cumulative_recognized_amount = cumsum(recognized_amount),

      cumulative_direct_payment_count = cumsum(direct_payment_count),
      cumulative_soft_credit_count = cumsum(soft_credit_count),

      active_giving_years = cumsum(recognized_amount > 0),

      peak_annual_giving_to_date = cummax(recognized_amount),

      prior_modern_gift_fy = na_if(
        lag(
          cummax(
            if_else(recognized_amount > 0, fiscal_year, 0L)
          ),
          default = 0L
        ),
        0L
      )
    ) |>
    ungroup() |>

    # Prior-year and next-year giving
    left_join(
      giving_lag1,
      by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")
    ) |>
    left_join(
      giving_lag2,
      by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")
    ) |>
    left_join(
      giving_next,
      by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")
    ) |>
    log_rows("+ prior and next-year giving") |>

    # All 23 solicitation features
    left_join(
      campaign_fy,
      by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")
    ) |>
    log_rows("+ 23 solicitation features") |>

    # Passport
    left_join(
      passport_fy,
      by = c("constituent_id", "fiscal_year")
    ) |>
    log_rows("+ Passport") |>

    # Spouse group
    left_join(
      select(individuals, constituent_id, split_group_id),
      by = "constituent_id"
    ) |>
    log_rows("+ spouse group id")
}

panel <- assemble_panel(feature_years, giving_year)
```

#### Engineer the Modeling Variables

```{r}
engineer_panel <- function(panel) {

  panel |>
    mutate(
      # Outcome-year giving
      across(
        starts_with("next_"),
        \(x) coalesce(x, 0)
      ),

      # Solicitation counts
      # Rates remain NA when their denominators are zero.
      across(
        c(
          solicitations,
          campaign_responses,
          campaign_codes_linked,
          unique_campaigns_solicited,
          solicitations_digital,
          solicitations_miscellaneous,
          solicitations_mail,
          solicitations_email,
          solicitations_phone,
          solicitations_in_person,
          responses_miscellaneous,
          responses_mail,
          responses_phone,
          responses_email,
          responses_digital,
          responses_in_person,
          prior_fy_solicitations,
          prior_fy_campaign_responses,
          trailing_3_fy_solicitations,
          trailing_3_fy_campaign_responses
        ),
        \(x) coalesce(x, 0)
      ),

      # Outcome and subgroup
      major_donor_next_fy = as.integer(
        next_recognized_amount >= major_threshold
      ),

      current_donor = as.integer(recognized_amount > 0),

      # Benchmark predictors
      log_current_giving = log1p(recognized_amount),

      log_peak_annual_giving = log1p(
        peak_annual_giving_to_date
      ),

      any_soft_credit_to_date = as.integer(
        cumulative_soft_amount > 0
      ),

      # Giving history
      prior_recognized_amount = if_else(
        fiscal_year == first_modern_fy,
        NA_real_,
        coalesce(recognized_lag1, 0)
      ),

      two_years_back = if_else(
        fiscal_year <= first_modern_fy + 1L,
        NA_real_,
        coalesce(recognized_lag2, 0)
      ),

      yoy_change = recognized_amount - prior_recognized_amount,

      trailing_three_year_slope = case_when(
        fiscal_year == first_modern_fy ~ NA_real_,

        fiscal_year == first_modern_fy + 1L ~
          recognized_amount - prior_recognized_amount,

        TRUE ~ (recognized_amount - two_years_back) / 2
      ),

      prior_giving_tier = amount_tier(
        prior_recognized_amount
      ),

      highest_giving_tier_to_date = amount_tier(
        peak_annual_giving_to_date
      ),

      cumulative_gift_count =
        cumulative_direct_payment_count +
        cumulative_soft_credit_count,

      average_gifts_per_active_year =
        cumulative_gift_count / pmax(active_giving_years, 1),

      average_recognized_per_active_year =
        cumulative_recognized_amount / pmax(active_giving_years, 1),

      # Giving recency
      prior_gift_fy = case_when(
        is.na(prior_modern_gift_fy) ~ legacy_last_gift_fy,

        is.na(legacy_last_gift_fy) ~ prior_modern_gift_fy,

        TRUE ~ pmax(
          prior_modern_gift_fy,
          legacy_last_gift_fy
        )
      ),

      years_since_prior_gift = fiscal_year - prior_gift_fy,

      no_prior_gift_known = as.integer(
        is.na(prior_gift_fy)
      ),

      # Passport
      passport_recorded = as.integer(
        !is.na(total_titles_viewed)
      )
    )
}

engineered <- engineer_panel(panel)
```
